title: LLMTailor: A Layer-wise Tailoring Tool for Efficient Checkpointing of Large Language Models
problem: Checkpointing for LLM training incurs substantial storage overhead and resource contention due to periodic full model+optimizer state storage; selective layer checkpointing is hampered by lack of fine-grained control tools.
motivation: Layer-wise updates are highly non-uniform during LLM training—some layers change significantly while others remain stable. Selective checkpointing can reduce overhead without harming training quality.
method: LLMTailor: a checkpoint-merging framework that filters and assembles layers from different checkpoints to form composite checkpoints, enabling selective strategies with fine-grained control over weights and optimizer states.
key_novelty: First tool enabling layer-wise selective checkpointing by merging composite checkpoints from heterogeneous layer updates; decouples checkpoint I/O from training pipeline.
contributions: Checkpoint-merging framework supporting selective layer strategies
Maintains training quality despite reduced checkpoint size
Fine-grained control over weights and optimizer states
limitations: Abstract-only; lacks detail on compatibility with different checkpoint formats, optimizer states heterogeneity, or convergence guarantees
